image_description: A disassembled bassoon resting horizontally inside an open, velvet-lined instrument case. The image shows the main body sections (boot, long joint, wing joint) and the bell section arranged in parallel rows. The wood is a deep reddish-brown with a polished finish, and numerous silver-plated metal keys and rods are visible. A metal ferrule or ring connects two sections in the foreground.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Long wooden wind instrument of considerable height when assembled.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The instrument is disassembled and lying in a case; its full assembled height cannot be verified from this static view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Distinctive U-shape when viewed from front with bell pointing upward.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The U-shape is a property of the assembled instrument. In the disassembled state shown, the 'U' structure is not visually present as a single connected form.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Conical bore that doubles back on itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Internal bore geometry and the doubling-back mechanism are internal features not visible in an external photograph of disassembled parts.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Curved metal bocal mouthpiece tube at top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bocal (the curved metal neck) is missing from the case layout; only the wooden body sections are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Numerous metal keys and tone holes distributed along length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Complex silver keywork, rods, and tone holes are clearly visible on the wooden sections, matching the intricate mechanical design of a bassoon.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bell flares outward at top and instrument held diagonally across body when played.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The 'held diagonally' checkpoint refers to playing posture, which is impossible to verify with an instrument in a case. The bell flare is partially visible but the context is wrong.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dark reddish-brown polished wood finish maple or rosewood.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The wood exhibits the characteristic deep reddish-brown hue and high-gloss polish typical of maple or rosewood bassoons.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Metal keys are silver or gold-plated.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The keywork reflects light with a silver/chrome appearance, consistent with nickel-silver or silver-plated brass used in bassoons.
The visible components are clearly turned wooden tubes with precise boring for keys, consistent with wind instrument construction.

artifact_observations.location: Wood grain on the lower long-joint section
artifact_observations.reasoning: The wood grain appears slightly smudged or painterly rather than having sharp, distinct fibrous details typical of high-resolution macro photography of polished wood. It lacks micro-contrast.

artifact_observations.location: Key mechanisms on the middle section
artifact_observations.reasoning: Several key rods and levers appear to merge into the wood body without clear mounting points or pivot screws. The geometry of the linkage system is vague and physically ambiguous, suggesting AI hallucination of complex mechanics.
The elliptical shape of the metal ring seems slightly inconsistent with the perspective of the cylindrical wood it surrounds, appearing slightly warped rather than a perfect ellipse.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific type of woodwind instrument and distinguish it from similar instruments like the contrabassoon or oboe based on keywork density and body thickness.
To audit the boundary between the metal keys and the wood body, checking for fusion artifacts where complex mechanical parts meet the wooden tube.
To assess the realism of the wood texture and the reflection properties of the metal keys, looking for subtle generative smoothness or noise patterns.
To verify the spatial relationship between the instrument parts and the case lining, ensuring no floating elements or incorrect depth ordering.

focus_areas: Integrity of metal keywork connections to wood body
Realism of wood grain texture vs. AI smoothing
Consistency of lighting reflections on metal vs. wood
